argument: As a Japan macro specialist, I challenge this XOM thesis on several fronts that intersect with my coverage: 1) **Yen Strength Risk**: USD/JPY has been volatile and if we see yen strengthening (which I expect given BOJ's gradual normalization), dollar-denominated energy assets like XOM face FX headwinds. Japanese corporates are major energy importers - stronger yen typically corresponds with weaker oil demand from Japan, putting pressure on WTI. 2) **China-Japan Trade Cycle**: The proposal mentions Permian growth but ignores Asia-Pacific demand dynamics. Japan's industrial production has been mixed, and any China slowdown (which affects my EWJ thesis) directly impacts refined product exports that XOM depends on. My EWJ/EFA ratio at -0.36 z-score suggests Japan is underperforming DM broadly, indicating weaker regional energy demand. 3) **Carry Trade Unwind Risk**: XOM's 44% 1Y performance coincides with massive carry trade flows. If BOJ continues tightening (my base case), carry unwinds could pressure high-beta energy names disproportionately. 4) **Missing Asia Catalyst**: The proposal lacks analysis of LNG dynamics crucial to XOM's integrated model. Japan's LNG import patterns are shifting post-Fukushima normalization, and this isn't addressed. The 8% vs 5% Permian growth differential seems optimistic without considering Asian demand destruction from potential yen strength. I'd want to see this hedged against energy demand proxies, not just RSPG.
